argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower defense than the original packet implied. Certification is supportable only as an aggregate-readiness decision: the release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.4 percentage points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance supports deployment with documented limitations plus ongoing measurement and monitoring. That same record does not prove the municipal permitting assistant disclosure issue is resolved. The defensible position is therefore not clean compliance on the disclosure question, but a bounded certification rationale that acknowledges an unresolved materiality dispute in the record.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to support this narrower position. The main point is evidentiary: aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support proceeding on a monitored basis, even though they do not close the disclosure question.
claims_about_policy: Public governance guidance on documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing monitoring helps justify certification in an overall-readiness sense, but it does not override the internal release policy. Under the stated policy text, the municipal permitting assistant weakness is plausibly material because the segment is named in two city pilot commitments, and the 7% projected traffic or non-core label does not by itself resolve materiality. The strongest policy-consistent reading is that the packet should avoid claiming the disclosure predicate is satisfied and instead present certification as a limited overall-readiness judgment with the disclosure issue explicitly preserved as unresolved.
concessions: No new evidence is being added.
There is no admissible evidence of approved pre-launch risk acceptance for the municipal permitting assistant limitation.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before certification.
There is no admissible evidence that the segment gap was remediated before launch.
The open legal ticket means the disclosure question remains unresolved in the present record.
The 7% projected traffic note does not itself defeat materiality for a named launch use case.
